keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria lacks (-323..-308). At the Partition of Babylon in 323 'a smaller north-west portion, principally around the Araxes River basin, went to Atropates'; the Atropatene page dates the founding c. 323 and has Atropates refuse allegiance to Seleucus 'shortly thereafter' and the Atropates page 'at some point thereafter'. The outline is Cliopatria's 307 shape, which reaches 38.7 N, short of the Araxes itself. The outline is Iranian Azerbaijan around Lake Urmia (the page: 'mostly centered around the present-day Azerbaijan region in northwestern Iran'); the page gives no area or boundary, so the area cannot be compared with an infobox figure.

region.text: north-west Media, the former sub-satrapy of Matiene, around the Araxes basin and Lake Urmia

ledger.note: 323: Atropates takes north-west Media at the Partition of Babylon and founds Atropatene. 'a smaller north-west portion, principally around the Araxes River basin, went to Atropates' (Atropates page); infobox 'c. 323 BC' (Atropatene page). He refuses allegiance at 'some point thereafter' (undated); the Atropatene page gives 321 (Triparadisus) no mention.

region.text: Atropatene, attacked by the Seleucid army

ledger.note: 221: Antiochus III attacks Atropatene. Antiochus 'attacked Atropatene, resulting in a victory'; the Antiochus III page orders it after Molon's revolt collapsed in 221 ('The submission of Lesser Media'). [Reviewer me-05-c, 2026-10-19: year corrected from 223; the Atropatene page body says only that Antiochus III came to power in 223 BCE, and its infobox map is captioned 'Atropatene as a vassal of Seleucids in 221 BC'.]
221: Artabazanes accepts Seleucid overlordship and keeps internal independence; the Seleucid Empire dossier records the vassal tint (counterpart atropatene, 221-190).

148: Mithridates I of Parthia invades Media and Atropatene. He 'conquered Media and Atropatene in 148/7 BC'; the body places the occupation of Ecbatana in 148 or 147 and then the conquest of Media Atropatene.
147: Atropatene is subdued and becomes an autonomous Parthian vassal ('Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire (148/7 BC-226 AD)'); the Parthian dossier records the vassal tint.

6: the Atropatid line gives way to the Arsacids. The rulers table ends the House of Atropates with Artavasdes II (r. 4-6 AD) and lists an Arsacid dynasty from Artabanus (to 12) and Vonones (12-51); the body speaks of 'the Parthian Arsacid supplantation of the Atropatid line in the early 1st century AD'. Same state and land; only the ruling house changes.

region.text: Atropatene, a province of the Sasanian Empire governed by a marzban

ledger.note: 226: Atropatene submits to Ardashir I. It 'submitted with little resistance to Ardashir I' in 226, after he killed Artabanus IV at the Battle of Hormozdgan, and 'became a province governed by a marzban'.
226: the kingdom of Atropatene ends. The local nobility allied with Ardashir partly to restore order; the infobox gives 226 AD as the end.

wars.name: Antiochus III's campaign against Atropatene
wars.outcome: Seleucid victory; Artabazanes accepts Seleucid overlordship but keeps internal independence.
wars.note: The Antiochus III page gives no year for 'The submission of Lesser Media' and puts it after 221.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Media and Atropatene
wars.outcome: Mithridates I conquers Media and Atropatene in 148/7; Atropatene remains an autonomous kingdom, frequently a Parthian vassal.

wars.name: Antony's Parthian campaign (siege of Phraaspa)
wars.outcome: In 36 BC Antony 'attacked Fraaspa' and withdrew after a long blockade, losing about thirty-five thousand soldiers.
wars.note: No territorial result; Atropatene later 'began to draw closer to Rome' as Parthia tried to annex it (undated).

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of Atropatene
wars.outcome: Atropatene submits with little resistance to Ardashir I after Hormozdgan and becomes a Sasanian province under a marzban.

notes:
Atropatene, group me-05-c. Three pages cited: Atropatene, Atropates and Mithridates I of Parthia (the last read for the Seleucid dossier). The Seleucid Empire and Antiochus III the Great pages, also read for the Seleucid dossier, supply the 223 and 221 context quoted in notes (page budget 5).

Decision for the reviewer: Cliopatria's row ends in 165, but the Atropatene page keeps the state alive to 226 ('Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire (148/7 BC-226 AD)'; Sasanian submission 226). The dossier therefore runs -323..226 with two new keyframes (-164..-149 autonomous; -148..225 Parthian-vassal period) that reuse Cliopatria's last outline. Cliopatria's Parthian shapes from 164 to 237 contain 578 of the 582 cells of that outline: the Parthian dossier (me-06) should either subtract Atropatene or draw it with the vassal tint; the Seleucid dossier carries the earlier vassal tint (vassal_start 221 to vassal_end 190, counterpart atropatene) and the Parthian dossier should carry 148/7 to 226.

Birth: Cliopatria begins in 307; the pages put the state at the Partition of Babylon in 323 (found c. 323; independence from the diadochi undated; Triparadisus 321 not on the pages). Cliopatria's 307 outline stops at 38.7 N, short of the Araxes basin the Atropates page names as the core of the 323 portion.

Disagreements: none on the year of Antiochus III's attack: the Atropatene infobox map gives 221 and the Antiochus III page puts it after 221 (the 223 of an earlier draft was Antiochus III's accession; corrected by the me-05-c review). No Seleucid-Atropatene border move is dated anywhere in 301-148 on the pages opened; the eleven Cliopatria shapes differ by under 0.5 percent of area and are all ok.

Not recorded: the Roman Republic's relation (Pompey: page silent; 36 BC Antony's blockade of Phraaspa is a war without territorial result); Artabazanes, Mithridates I, Darius I and later kings of the House of Atropates (the infobox gives floruit dates only, so no ruler strip); the Iberian devastation of 134-135 AD (undated reach).

Gazetteer: Ganzak and Phraaspa are not in places.jsonl (capital coordinates are given directly).
